name: Black Bean
lede: Black Bean is a near-black, reddish brown named for the dried legume, a shade darker and redder than ordinary chocolate brown.

sections.title: A legume's name, no documented coining
sections.body:
Our library traces the name only to a Wikipedia color list, which cites no book, dictionary or date for who coined it [1]. The ISCC-NBS system, which assigns descriptive names to measured blocks of color, calls this swatch a dark reddish brown [1]. Measured in LCH, it sits at lightness 11, close to black, with a modest reddish-orange hue angle [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[dark-sienna]], 4.1 units of CIEDE2000 away and described as duller and redder [1]. [[oxblood]] sits a little farther off, at 4.4, and is more vivid [1]. Against those two, and against the paler [[dark-sienna]] and the lighter [[carbuncle]], Black Bean reads as the quietest, darkest member of the group [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 945 of 23,781 paintings (4.0 percent), more common than 79 percent of the named colors, as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1400s, in 33 of 945 paintings, at 2.1 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a shadow, 48 percent of the time, a role measured by lightness rank within the canvas rather than by the raw hex match [2]. It shares canvases with Maroon and Burnt Red more often than chance [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment identification [2].
